info.title: Edge CLI
info.description: The `edge-cli` command line and the `edge-engine` JSON REST API, generated from the route declarations in `src/cli/engine/routes/`.

servers.description: Loopback TCP, when started with --tcp=9008. Requires the X-Edge-Token header; see securitySchemes.

tags.name: Lifecycle
tags.description: Lifecycle and configuration of the `edge-engine` daemon. None of these have an `edge-core-js` equivalent — they describe the daemon itself — and none need a session.

tags.name: Device and usernames
tags.description: Calls on the shared `EdgeContext`: local device state and login-server queries that do not need a session.

tags.name: Login methods
tags.description: Every successful login returns a [Session](#schema-Session) and registers it in the engine, so later calls need only the `sessionId`. The CLI writes that id to `session.json` automatically.

tags.name: Session
tags.description: Calls on a logged-in `EdgeAccount`, addressed by `sessionId`. All of these can also return `401 INVALID_SESSION` or `401 SESSION_EXPIRED`.

tags.name: Object handles
tags.description: A core value with methods on it — a staged transaction, a swap quote, a pending login — cannot cross JSON, so the engine keeps it and hands back an id. These read and release any of them.

tags.name: Event stream
tags.description: A Server-Sent Events feed of engine activity, served outside the router because the response never ends.

get.description:
**Core call:** _none — Engine lifecycle; the daemon is not part of the core API._

**Command line**

```
engine-status
```

The readiness probe the client polls after auto-spawning the engine.
get.x-core-note: Engine lifecycle; the daemon is not part of the core API.

200.description: Every field is documented on `asEngineStatus`; the two nullable ones, `idleShutdownAt` and `tcpPort`, say there what null means.

pid.description: The daemon process, for `kill` when it will not stop.

apiVersion.description: The API this engine speaks. A client refusing to talk to an older engine checks this.

uptimeSeconds.description: How long the daemon has been running.

sessionCount.description: Logged-in accounts held open right now.

testMode.description: True when the engine is not pointed at production: the tester fleet, or the in-process fake world under `--fake`.

idleShutdownAt.description: When the engine will exit for want of work. Null while a client is deliberately holding it open — a logged-in session, a live subscription, or a handle that belongs to no session (a pending edge login, or a parked admin lobby) — and null when the timeout is disabled. A request being served also disarms the timer, but is not reported here: the request asking for this field is itself in flight.

tcpPort.description: The loopback port, null unless started with `--tcp`.

socketPath.description: Unix socket the CLI connects to.

rateCachedCount.description: Exchange rates held in the engine’s process cache. It is bounded and cleared when the last session goes away, and this is how an operator sees it.

rateUnpricedCount.description: Rate keys the server answered without a price, remembered for a few minutes so a repeated listing does not re-ask for every date. A number that stays high means an asset with no feed on the rates server — a hand-added custom token, a long-tail token, or dates predating its market.

locale.description: Language tag the engine resolved at boot.

localeMatched.description: Whether a translation table for that tag was actually found. False means the tag was accepted but the engine is answering in English, which is otherwise indistinguishable from a build that has the language.

get.description:
**Core call:** _none — Reflects the EdgeContextOptions the engine supplied at startup._

**Command line**

```
engine-config
```

What the engine passed to `makeEdgeContext`. Contains no secrets. Use it to assert tester hosts before a test run.
get.x-core-note: Reflects the EdgeContextOptions the engine supplied at startup.

appId.description: Application ID the engine was started with.

testMode.description: True when the engine is not pointed at production: the tester fleet, or the in-process fake world under `--fake`. Read `servers` to tell those apart.

directory.description: Working directory holding the core data.

servers.description: The URLs this engine talks to, keyed by role. `syncServer` is a list, since core rotates across the sync fleet.

plugins.description: Plugin IDs the engine loaded, sorted.

configFiles.description: Where this engine’s configuration came from. The profile a client hashes covers `appId`, the data directory, test mode and the login server — not these, so two invocations with the same flags from different directories share one daemon, and this is what says which configuration it is running on.

post.description:
**Core call:** _none — Engine lifecycle. Internally calls `context.close()`._

**Command line**

```
engine-stop
```

Logs out every session, closes the context, unlinks the socket and run-file, then exits. The engine answers before it starts tearing down, so a response is not proof the process is gone.

ok.description: Always true; a failure arrives as an error envelope.

get.summary: List local users on this device.

200.description: Everything `context.localUsers` reports, including which login methods each user has enabled on this device.

localUsers.description: `EdgeUserInfo[]`: one entry per account cached on this device.

post.summary: Forget an account on this device.
post.description:
**Core call:** `context.forgetAccount`

**Command line**


Removes locally cached credentials. The remote account is untouched.

rootLoginId.description: Core takes a `rootLoginId`. A username is also accepted and resolved against `localUsers` first, so callers need not hash it.

get.summary: Check whether a username is free.

parameters.name: username

parameters.name: challengeId
parameters.description: Supply after solving a CAPTCHA to retry the same check.

available.description: True when nobody holds this name. It is not reserved by asking.

get.description:
**Core call:** `context.fixUsername`

**Command line**

```
fix-username --username=<username>
```

Applies the same rules the login server does, so a caller can show the user what their name will actually be before creating an account.

parameters.description: The name to normalize.

post.description:
**Core call:** `context.checkPasswordRules`

**Command line**

```
check-password-rules --password=<password>
```

`POST` with the candidate in the body. A query string is the one place a secret is written down by everything that touches it — the engine's own log redacts query values for that reason — and a URL is what a proxy, a crash report and a shell history keep. Nothing reads this route's result from a cache, so the method costs nothing.

200.description: `EdgePasswordRules` from core: passed, tooShort, noNumber, noLowerCase, noUpperCase, secondsToCrack.

get.summary: Fetch login-server messages for every local user.

200.description: An `EdgeLoginMessage[]` from core: one entry per local login, each with its own `loginId`, `otpResetPending`, `pendingVouchers`, `recovery2Corrupt` and, where the stash has one, `username`. `loginId` is base58, like every other login id in this API — core answers it in base64 here, and an id in the wrong alphabet is one `forget-account` and `--use-login-id` reject.

post.description:
**Core call:** `context.requestEdgeLogin`

**Command line**

```
request-edge-login [--no-wait]
```

Asks the login server for a lobby another logged-in Edge device can approve. The returned `lobbyId` is what goes in the QR code.

extra.name: no-wait
extra.doc: Print the lobby and exit instead of polling, so the QR can be displayed while `poll-edge-login` watches the same handle from another process.

x-cli.notes: Prints the pending login, then polls every 2s for up to 5 minutes. On `done` it stores the session. With `--no-wait` it returns immediately and `poll-edge-login` takes over.

objectId.description: Handle for the value the engine is holding. Pass it to the calls that consume it.

pendingId.description: Same value as `objectId`, under the name the poll command takes.

kind.description: What the handle refers to, which decides the calls that accept it.

expiresAt.description: When the lobby closes and the QR code stops working.

uri.description: The `edge://` URI to render as a QR code for the phone to scan.

state.description: How far the login has got: `pending` before the phone scans, `started` once it has, and `done` when `session` is filled in.

username.description: Account that approved the login, known once the phone has scanned.

error.description: Why the login failed, set only when `state` is `error`.

post.summary: Wait for every wallet to finish loading.
post.description:
**Core call:** `account.waitForAllWallets`

**Command line**

```
wait-for-all-wallets
```

Wallets load in the background after login, so a list taken straight afterwards can be short. This resolves once each active wallet has either loaded or failed — balances may still be syncing afterwards.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: From a successful login. The CLI supplies this from `session.json`, `--session`, or `EDGE_CLI_SESSION`.

unloadedWallets.description: The active wallets core did *not* build an API for, each with its `walletId`, `walletType`, `pluginId`, `pluginRegistered` and `pluginHasLoadedWallet`. Empty is the healthy answer. This call used to return nothing, so an account with a wallet the CLI cannot load got `ok` and a short `currency-wallets` list with no explanation. The engine cannot say *why* core declined — a registered plugin can still fail to build an engine, and in a Node CLI that is usually a native module the package does not carry — so what it says is this: `pluginRegistered: false` means no plugin claims that wallet type at all, and `pluginHasLoadedWallet: false` means nothing of that type loaded, so the plugin is the common factor rather than these wallets. The reason itself, when a plugin reports one, is in `~/.edge-cli/logs/engine-<profile>.log`, or in `engine-<profile>-startup.log` where a plugin’s own stderr lands; `EDGE_CLI_LOG_LEVEL=info` keeps core’s own chatter as well.

get.description:
**Core call:** `account.currencyWallets`

**Command line**

```
currency-wallets
```

Every wallet core has built an API for, which is the account's active set: `activeWalletIds` is `ids.filter(id => !archived)`, so an archived or deleted wallet is not here. Paused wallets are.

This took a `filter` of `active`, `archived`, `hidden` or `all`, and three of those four could not work. The handler resolved each id through `account.currencyWallets`, which core builds from `activeWalletIds` **alone**, so the archived and hidden lists were disjoint from the resolvable set by construction: every id mapped to `undefined`, the `filter(wallet != null)` dropped it, and `?filter=archived` answered `{"currencyWallets":[]}` on every account, always. `all` concatenated the three lists, so it was `active` with each hidden wallet — which is active and hidden at once, core deriving the two flags independently — listed twice. Nor could the missing wallets be served in this shape: an archived wallet has no loaded API, so `name`, `currencyCode`, `blockHeight`, `syncStatus` and `paused` do not exist for it, and seven required response fields would have had to become nullable for every caller to carry three values that never worked.

`all-keys` is the route for that, and already was: it returns `EdgeWalletInfoFull[]` — id, type, `archived`, `deleted`, `hidden`, `sortIndex` — which is everything knowable about a wallet core has not loaded.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: From a successful login. The CLI supplies this from `session.json`, `--session`, or `EDGE_CLI_SESSION`.

currencyWallets.description: Every wallet core has loaded for this account, including paused ones. Archived, deleted and hidden wallets are not loaded; `all-keys` lists those.

unloadedWallets.description: The active wallets that are *not* in the list above, each with its `walletId`, `walletType`, `pluginId`, `pluginRegistered` and `pluginHasLoadedWallet`. Before `wait-for-all-wallets` an entry here may simply still be building; after it, it has failed. They used to be filtered out silently, so this list was the difference between `all-keys` and this one and a caller had to compute it — and nothing said why a wallet was missing. See `wait-for-all-wallets` for what the two plugin fields do and do not claim.

post.description:
**Core call:** `account.createCurrencyWallet`

**Command line**

```
create-currency-wallet --wallet-type=<walletType> [--name=<name>] [--import-text=<importText>]
```

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: From a successful login. The CLI supplies this from `session.json`, `--session`, or `EDGE_CLI_SESSION`.

walletId.description: The full wallet id. Commands taking a wallet accept any unique prefix.

id.description: Same value as `walletId`, under the name `edge-core-js` uses. Core’s `EdgeCurrencyWallet` has only `id`; `walletId` is the name every route’s parameter takes, so both are published and a caller can use whichever half of the API it is reading.

name.description: User-assigned name, null until one is set.

fiatCurrencyCode.description: Fiat the wallet reports value in, as `iso:USD`.

blockHeight.description: Chain height this wallet has seen.

syncRatio.description: Sync progress as a percentage, for display.

paused.description: True while the engine is not syncing this wallet.

imported.description: True when the keys came from an import rather than being generated here.

created.description: When the wallet was created, null for wallets predating the field.

detectedTokenIds.description: Tokens found on-chain that are not enabled yet.

unactivatedTokenIds.description: Enabled tokens still awaiting on-chain activation.

importText.description: Seed or key text to import instead of generating.

post.description:
**Core call:** `account.createCurrencyWallets`

**Core call:** _none — Engine-side fan-out; `core.log` frames carry core's onLog output._

**Command line**

```
subscribe [--session-id=<sessionId>] [--wallet-id=<walletId>] [--type=<type> …]
```

Holds a Server-Sent Events stream open until the caller disconnects or the engine closes it. Runs concurrently with one-shot calls, so a subscriber in one terminal watches what another terminal does.

A live subscription holds the engine open past its idle timeout. It does not hold an account logged in: the auto-logout timer still fires, and closes any subscription scoped to that account or one of its wallets. Context-scoped subscriptions survive, because the context outlives every account.

Scope comes from the query string. With no `sessionId` the stream is context-scoped and nothing but the engine stopping ends it, which is what the `subscribe` command asks for. With `sessionId` it is account-scoped: a logout closes it, and the session events of *other* accounts are filtered out. `walletId` narrows it further *within* that account, for whenever a wallet-scoped event exists: no event carries a wallet scope today, so it changes nothing a caller receives, and a wallet-scoped stream gets exactly what the same stream without `walletId` would have got. It is accepted now so a caller's URL does not have to change when the first such event arrives.

extra.name: type
extra.doc: Only these event types. Applied by the engine, so an unwanted type never crosses the socket; the client filters again for the types the engine sends regardless, like `subscription.closed`.

x-cli.notes: Prints newline-delimited JSON and runs until interrupted. Exits 0 on SIGINT and 7 when the engine ends the stream. `subscribe` opens an unscoped stream, which only the engine stopping ends; a stream opened with `sessionId` is closed by that session logging out.

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Scope the stream to one account, so a logout closes it. Omitted, the stream is context-scoped and only the engine stopping ends it.

parameters.name: walletId
parameters.description: With `sessionId`, narrow the stream to one wallet. No event carries a wallet scope yet, so today this changes nothing you receive — the stream still carries every account event the same `sessionId` alone would carry. Ignored on its own.

200.description: One frame per event, as `event:` then `data:` lines.

data.description: Payload, shaped by the event type.

edgeTcpToken.name: X-Edge-Token
edgeTcpToken.description: The bearer token the engine mints for its loopback TCP listener, written to the `0600` run file at ~/.edge-cli/run/<profile>/engine.json as `tcpToken`. Required on the TCP transport and ignored on the unix socket. A TCP request that also carries `Origin`, or a `Host` other than the bound address, is refused with 403 whatever token it presents.
